subject: Biology
title: CHAPTER 13: PLANT GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT (NEST & INBO MODULE)
description: Comprehensive master module covering Seed Germination Physiology, Dormancy Breakage Mechanics, Mathematical Growth Kinetics (Arithmetic vs Geometric), Differentiation / Dedifferentiation / Redifferentiation, Plasticity & Heterophylly, The 5 Major Phytohormones (Auxins, Gibberellins, Cytokinins, Ethylene, ABA), Photoperiodism, Phytochromes (Pr vs Pfr), Vernalization, High-Yield Traps, Master Glossary, and 20 NEST Practice Questions.

sections.title: Seed Germination Physiology & Dormancy Breakage Mechanics
sections.topic: Epigeal vs Hypogeal Germination, Imbibition, Scarification & Stratification

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Germination begins with passive imbibition triggering GA secretion. Scarification breaks physical dormancy; Stratification (cold moist 0–5°C) breaks physiological dormancy by shifting ABA/GA balance.

sections.codeSnippet:
SEED GERMINATION PHASES
                                    │
  Imbibition (Passive Water Uptake) ──► Metabolic Activation (GA Release)
                                              │
  Radicle Emergence (Cell Elongation) ◄── α-Amylase Synthesis & Starch Hydrolysis

                      EPIGEAL vs HYPOGEAL GERMINATION
                      
      EPIGEAL GERMINATION (*Castor / Bean*)      HYPOGEAL GERMINATION (*Maize / Pea*)
      ├── Hypocotyl elongates rapidly            ├── Epicotyl elongates rapidly
      └── Cotyledons pulled ABOVE soil           └── Cotyledons remain BELOW soil
sections.content:
Seed germination is the resumption of metabolic activity and growth by a quiescent embryonic axis, culminating in the emergence of the radicle through the seed coat.

### 1.1 Germination Types & Physiological Events
1. **Epigeal Germination**: The hypocotyl elongates rapidly, forming a hook that pulls the cotyledons above the soil surface (*Castor, Cotton, Mustard, Bean*).
2. **Hypogeal Germination**: The epicotyl elongates while the hypocotyl remains short, leaving the cotyledons below the soil surface (*Maize, Wheat, Gram, Pea*).

### 1.2 Seed Dormancy & Breakage Mechanisms
Seed dormancy is an evolutionary state of suppressed germination even when optimal environmental conditions (water, oxygen, temperature) are met.
- **Physical Dormancy**: Impermeable, rigid seed coat (lignified/suberized) in *Legumes, Malvaceae*.
- **Chemical Dormancy**: Endogenous inhibitors (Abscisic Acid, Coumarin, Ferulic Acid).
- **Physiological Dormancy**: Immature embryo requiring chilling or photoperiodic maturation.

#### Dormancy Breakage Techniques:
1. **Scarification**: Mechanical chipping, abrasion, or chemical treatment with concentrated sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) to rupture impermeable seed coats.
2. **Stratification**: Subjecting moist seeds to cold temperature treatment ($0\text{--}5^\circ\text{C}$) under aerobic conditions to lower Abscisic Acid (ABA) levels and elevate Gibberellin ($\text{GA}$) biosynthesis.
3. **Light / Phytochromes**: Exposing photoblastic seeds (e.g., Lettuce - *Lactuca sativa*) to red light ($660\text{ nm}$).

sections.title: Phases of Plant Growth & Mathematical Growth Rates
sections.topic: Meristematic, Elongation, Maturation Phases & Arithmetic vs Geometric Kinetics

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Arithmetic growth is linear ($L_t = L_0 + rt$). Geometric growth yields a Sigmoid S-curve ($W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$) with lag, log/exponential, and stationary phases.

sections.codeSnippet:
MATHEMATICAL GROWTH MODELS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   ARITHMETIC GROWTH                                      GEOMETRIC GROWTH
   Only ONE daughter cell divides while                   BOTH daughter cells retain mitotic
   the other differentiates.                              capacity ($2^n$ proliferation).
   ├── Equation: $L_t = L_0 + rt$                         ├── Equation: $W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$
   └── Graph: **Linear Curve**                            └── Graph: **Sigmoidal (S) Curve**

                        SIGMOIDAL (S) GROWTH CURVE
                        
           Size/Weight ▲                       Stationary Phase
                       │                      /----------------
                       │                     /
                       │   Exponential /    /
                       │   Log Phase       /
                       │                  /
                       │  Lag Phase      /
                       └────────────────┴──────────────────────► Time
sections.content:
Plant growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size, mass, or volume of an organ or cell, accompanied by metabolic synthetic processes.

### Phases of Growth
1. **Meristematic Phase**: Isodiametric, thin-walled, dense cytoplasm, prominent nuclei (*Root/Shoot apex*).
2. **Elongation Phase**: Rapid vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.
3. **Maturation Phase**: Maximal wall thickening, structural and functional differentiation.

### 2.1 Arithmetic vs. Geometric Growth Models
- **Arithmetic Growth**: $L_t = L_0 + rt$ where $L_t$ is length at time $t$, $L_0$ is initial length, and $r$ is the constant elongation rate per unit time.
- **Geometric Growth**: $W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$ where $W_1$ is final size/weight, $W_0$ is initial size, $r$ is relative growth rate (efficiency index), $t$ is time, and $e \approx 2.718$.

### 2.2 Absolute vs. Relative Growth Rates
- **Absolute Growth Rate (AGR)**: Total growth per unit time ($AGR = \frac{\Delta W}{\Delta t}$).
- **Relative Growth Rate (RGR)**: Growth per unit time relative to initial size ($RGR = \frac{AGR}{W_0}$).

sections.title: Cellular Differentiation, Dedifferentiation, Redifferentiation, & Plasticity
sections.topic: Permanent Cell Specialization, Secondary Meristem Regain, & Heterophylly

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Meristem ➔ Permanent (Differentiation) ➔ Secondary Meristem (Dedifferentiation) ➔ Secondary Permanent Tissue (Redifferentiation). Plasticity is seen in developmental & environmental heterophylly.

sections.codeSnippet:
DEVELOPMENTAL CELLULAR STATES
                                     │
  Meristematic Cell ──[DIFFERENTIATION]──► Mature Permanent Cell (*Tracheid*)
                                                   │
  Secondary Meristem ◄──[DEDIFFERENTIATION]───────┘ (*Interfascicular Cambium*)
          │
          └──[REDIFFERENTIATION]──► Secondary Tissue (*Secondary Xylem / Cork*)
sections.content:
Plant development involves orderly structural and functional transitions:

1. **Differentiation**: The structural and functional specialization of meristematic cells accompanied by loss of division capacity (e.g., formation of a tracheary element involves loss of protoplasm and deposition of lignified secondary walls).
2. **Dedifferentiation**: The phenomenon by which fully mature, differentiated, non-dividing living cells regain the capacity for mitotic division under specific cues (e.g., formation of Interfascicular Cambium and Cork Cambium / Phellogen from parenchyma cells).
3. **Redifferentiation**: The process by which cells produced by secondary meristems lose their division capacity once again to become functionally mature secondary tissues (e.g., Secondary Xylem, Secondary Phloem, Phellem, Phelloderm).
4. **Plasticity & Heterophylly**:
   - **Developmental Heterophylly**: Leaf shapes differ between juvenile and adult phases (*Cotton, Coriander, Larkspur*).
   - **Environmental Heterophylly**: Leaf shapes differ between aquatic and terrestrial environments (*Buttercup - Ranunculus flabellaris*).

sections.title: Phytohormone I: Auxins
sections.topic: IAA, Polar Auxin Transport (PAT), Acid Growth Hypothesis, & Apical Dominance

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Auxin (IAA) is biosynthesized from Tryptophan with Zn²⁺. Drives cell elongation via Acid Growth Hypothesis (H⁺-ATPase), apical dominance, and rooting; 2,4-D is a selective dicot herbicide.

sections.codeSnippet:
POLAR AUXIN TRANSPORT (PAT) MECHANISM
                     
   Auxin enters cell as uncharged **IAAH** ──► Dissociates in neutral cytosol to **IAA⁻**
                                                                   │
   Directional Efflux ◄── PIN Efflux Carrier Proteins localized at BASAL membrane

                        ACID GROWTH HYPOTHESIS
                        
   Auxin binds PM Receptor ──► Activates Plasma Membrane $H^+$-ATPase Proton Pump
                                           │
   Expansins Activated ◄── Wall Acidified (pH ~4.5) ──► $H^+$ pumped into Cell Wall
            │
   Cell Wall Loosening ──► Turgor-driven Cell Elongation
sections.content:
Auxins (from Greek *auxein* = to grow) are weakly acidic phytohormones characterized by an unsaturated ring structure containing an acidic side chain.

### Auxin Classification
- **Natural Auxins**: Indole-3-acetic acid ($\text{IAA}$), Indole-3-butyric acid ($\text{IBA}$).
- **Synthetic Auxins**: $\alpha$-Naphthaleneacetic acid ($\text{NAA}$), 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid ($\text{2,4-D}$), 2,4,5-Trichlorophenoxyacetic acid ($\text{2,4,5-T}$).

### Biosynthesis & Bioassays
- **Precursor**: Biosynthesized from the amino acid L-Tryptophan requiring $\text{Zn}^{2+}$.
- **Bioassays**: Avena Coleoptile Curvature Test (Frits Went, 1928) and Root Growth Inhibition Test.

### Physiological Roles & Applications
1. **Apical Dominance**: High auxin concentrations from the shoot apex inhibit lateral axillary bud outgrowth. Decapitation triggers lateral branching (tea plantations, hedge pruning).
2. **Cell Elongation**: Activates plasma membrane $\text{H}^+$-ATPase pumps, lowering cell wall pH to $\sim 4.5$ and activating expansins (**Acid Growth Hypothesis**).
3. **Root Initiation**: Promotes adventitious root formation in stem cuttings ($\text{IBA}, \text{NAA}$).
4. **Selective Herbicide**: $\text{2,4-D}$ selectively kills broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds without affecting monocots.
5. **Parthenocarpy**: Induces seedless fruit development in tomatoes.

sections.title: Phytohormone II: Gibberellins
sections.topic: Bakanae Discovery, GA₃ Aleurone α-Amylase Induction, Bolting, & Sugarcane Yield

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Gibberellins (GA₃) derived from ent-kaurene induce α-amylase in aleurone layers via GAMYB, stimulate bolting in rosette plants, elongate sugarcane stems, and accelerate malting.

sections.codeSnippet:
GIBBERELLIN ALEURONE CASCADE
                      
   Germinating Embryo ──► Secretes Gibberellins ($\text{GA}_3$) into Endosperm
                                      │
   Target Layer       ──► $\text{GA}_3$ binds receptors in **Aleurone Layer** cells
                                      │
   Gene Expression    ──► De-represses GAMYB transcription factor ──► Transcribes **$\alpha$-Amylase**
                                      │
   Hydrolysis         ──► $\alpha$-Amylase degrades Starch ──► Glucose nourishes Embryo
sections.content:
Gibberellins (GAs) are complex tetracyclic diterpenoid acids derived from the ent-kaurene pathway. Over 100 GAs are known; $\text{GA}_3$ is the most widely studied.

### Discovery & Precursor
- Discovered by E. Kurosawa (1926) from *Bakanae* ("Foolish Seedling") Disease of rice caused by *Gibberella fujikuroi* (*Fusarium moniliforme*).
- Biosynthesized from Mevalonic Acid / Isopentenyl Pyrophosphate (IPP) via the Ent-Kaurene pathway.
- **Bioassays**: Barley Endosperm $\alpha$-Amylase Induction Test and Dwarf Pea/Maize Shoot Elongation Test.

### Physiological Roles
1. **Bolting in Rosette Plants**: Induces dramatic internodal stem elongation prior to flowering in rosette plants (*Cabbage, Sugarbeet, Henbane*).
2. **Malt Yield Acceleration**: Speeds up malting in brewing by stimulating hydrolytic enzyme secretion in germinating barley.
3. **Increasing Crop Dimensions**: Increases length of grape stalks (*Vitis*), improves apple fruit shape, and extends sugarcane stems (boosting sugar yield up to $20\text{ tonnes/acre}$).
4. **Delaying Senescence**: Delays fruit ripening on trees, extending market shelf-life (*Citrus*).

sections.title: Phytohormone III: Cytokinins
sections.topic: Zeatin vs Kinetin, Skoog-Miller Organogenesis Ratios, & Richmond-Lang Effect

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Cytokinins (Zeatin/Kinetin) promote cytokinesis and delay senescence (Richmond-Lang effect). High Cytokinin:Auxin induces Shoots; High Auxin:Cytokinin induces Roots.

sections.codeSnippet:
AUXIN : CYTOKININ RATIO OUTCOMES
                   
   High Auxin : Low Cytokinin   ──► Induces **ROOT DIFFERENTIATION (Rhizogenesis)**
   Low Auxin : High Cytokinin   ──► Induces **SHOOT DIFFERENTIATION (Caulogenesis)**
   Balanced Auxin : Cytokinin   ──► Maintains **CALLUS PROLIFERATION** (Undifferentiated mass)
sections.content:
Cytokinins are basic $N^6$-substituted adenine (purine) derivatives that promote cytokinesis (cell division) in the presence of auxin.

### Types & Discovery
- **Kinetin (Synthetic)**: $N^6$-furfurylaminopurine, isolated by Skoog & Miller (1955) from autoclaved herring sperm DNA.
- **Zeatin (Natural)**: $N^6$-(4-hydroxy-3-methylbut-2-enylamino)purine, isolated from corn kernels (*Zea mays*) and coconut milk.
- **Bioassays**: Tobacco Pith Tissue Culture Callus Assay and Radish Cotyledon Expansion Test.

### Morphogenic Auxin-to-Cytokinin Ratio (Skoog & Miller)
- **High Auxin : Low Cytokinin**: Induces **Root Differentiation (Rhizogenesis)**.
- **Low Auxin : High Cytokinin**: Induces **Shoot Differentiation (Caulogenesis)**.
- **Balanced Auxin : Cytokinin**: Maintains undifferentiated **Callus Proliferation**.

### Physiological Roles
1. **Delay of Leaf Senescence (Richmond-Lang Effect)**: Delays chlorophyll degradation and protein breakdown by mobilizing nutrients into treated tissues.
2. **Overcoming Apical Dominance**: Direct application to lateral axillary buds promotes their outgrowth, antagonizing auxin.
3. **Adventitious Shoot Formation**: Stimulates lateral shoot development in tissue culture.

sections.title: Phytohormone IV: Ethylene
sections.topic: Gaseous Ethylene Biosynthesis from Methionine, Triple Response, & Climacteric Ripening

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Ethylene is the only gaseous hormone (derived from Methionine via ACC). Causes the seedling Triple Response, climacteric fruit ripening, petiole elongation in submerged rice, and female flower induction.

sections.codeSnippet:
ETHYLENE TRIPLE RESPONSE
                        
   1. Inhibition of stem elongation (Shortened hypocotyl).
   2. Swelling and radial thickening of the hypocotyl axis.
   3. Horizontal geotropic growth with exaggerated **Apical Hook** formation.
sections.content:
Ethylene ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$) is a simple, volatile, gaseous phytohormone produced by ripening fruits and senescing tissues.

### Discovery & Biosynthesis
- Discovered by H.H. Cousins (1910) showing volatile gas from ripe oranges accelerated banana ripening.
- **Biosynthetic Precursor**: L-Methionine $\rightarrow$ S-Adenosylmethionine (SAM) $\rightarrow$ 1-Aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC) $\rightarrow$ Ethylene (catalyzed by ACC Oxidase).
- **Commercial Form (Ethephon)**: 2-chloroethylphosphonic acid, an aqueous formulation releasing ethylene gas inside tissues.
- **Bioassay**: Triple Response Bioassay on Etiolated Pea Seedlings.

### Physiological Roles
1. **Climacteric Fruit Ripening**: Triggers respiratory surge (Climacteric Rise), starch breakdown, and fruit softening (*Apple, Banana, Tomato, Mango*).
2. **Abscission & Defoliation**: Induces cellulase and pectinase enzymes in the abscission zone of leaves, flowers, and fruits.
3. **Promoting Feminization**: Increases proportion of female (pistillate) flowers in monoecious plants like Cucumber.
4. **Submerged Stem Elongation**: Promotes rapid petiole and internodal elongation in deep-water rice varieties.
5. **Root Hair Initiation**: Promotes root growth and root hair formation, expanding absorption surface area.

sections.title: Phytohormone V: Abscisic Acid (ABA)
sections.topic: Stress Hormone Dynamics, Guard Cell Stomatal Closure Mechanics, & GA Antagonism

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: ABA is a sesquiterpenoid stress hormone derived from violaxanthin. Triggers Ca²⁺ influx and K⁺/Cl⁻ efflux to close stomata during drought, and directly antagonizes Gibberellins in seed dormancy.

sections.codeSnippet:
ABA-MEDIATED STOMATAL CLOSURE
                      
   Water Deficit ──► Leaf ABA Rises ──► Binds Guard Cell Plasma Membrane Receptors
                                                      │
   Hyperpolarization ◄── Depolarization & $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ Influx into Guard Cell Cytosol
            │
   Efflux of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ Ions ──► Loss of Guard Cell Turgor ──► STOMATA CLOSE

                      GIBBERELLIN vs ABSCISIC ACID ANTAGONISM
                      
      GIBBERELLINS ($\text{GA}_3$)                 ABSCISIC ACID (ABA)
      ├── Breaks seed dormancy                    ├── Induces & maintains seed dormancy
      ├── Stimulates $\alpha$-Amylase synthesis   ├── Suppresses $\alpha$-Amylase synthesis
      └── Promotes growth & germination           └── Inhibits growth; promotes stomatal closure
sections.content:
Abscisic Acid (ABA) is a 15-carbon sesquiterpenoid phytohormone universally recognized as the master Stress Hormone and plant growth inhibitor.

### Discovery & Precursor
- Discovered independently by Addicott, Carns, and Wareing as *Abscisin II* and *Dormin*.
- Biosynthesized via oxidative cleavage of Carotenoid Xanthophylls (Violaxanthin).
- **Bioassays**: Stomatal Closure Bioassay and Rice Seedling Growth Inhibition Test.

### Stomatal Closure Mechanism
During water deficit, root-derived ABA binds guard cell receptors $\rightarrow$ activates $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ channels $\rightarrow$ cytosolic $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ surge depolarizes membrane $\rightarrow$ triggers rapid efflux of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions $\rightarrow$ guard cells lose turgor and stomata close.

### Physiological Roles
1. **Seed Dormancy Maintenance**: Directly antagonizes Gibberellins ($\text{GA}$) to suppress precocious germination.
2. **Stress Tolerance**: Induces synthesis of protective osmoprotectants and Late Embryogenesis Abundant (LEA) proteins under drought, salinity, and cold.

sections.title: Photoperiodism, Phytochrome Reversibility, & Vernalization
sections.topic: SDP vs LDP vs DNP Night Interruption, Pr/Pfr Interconversions, Florigen (FT), & FLC Epigenetics

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: SDPs are long-night plants (red flash in dark inhibits flowering). Leaves perceive photoperiod via Phytochromes (Pr ⇌ Pfr) and send Florigen (FT protein) to apex. Meristems perceive cold in Vernalization.

sections.codeSnippet:
PHYTOCHROME REVERSIBILITY
                        
               Red Light ($660\text{ nm}$)
               ─────────────────────────►
   P_r (Inactive Form)                     P_fr (Active Form)
   [Absorbs $660\text{ nm}$] ◄───────────────────────── [Absorbs $730\text{ nm}$]
               Far-Red Light ($730\text{ nm}$) / Dark Decay

   SHORT-DAY PLANT (SDP):   [   Day   ] [   Uninterrupted Long Night   ] ──► FLOWERING
                            [   Day   ] [   Night   | Flash |  Night   ] ──► NO FLOWERING
                            
   LONG-DAY PLANT (LDP):    [   Day   ] [   Night   | Flash |  Night   ] ──► FLOWERING
sections.content:
### 9.1 Photoperiodism (Garner & Allard, 1920)
Photoperiodism is the physiological response to the relative lengths of light and dark periods regulating flowering.
- **Short-Day Plants (SDP)**: Require night length exceeding critical duration (*Tobacco, Soybean, Cocklebur*). A brief flash of red light during the night **inhibits** flowering.
- **Long-Day Plants (LDP)**: Require light exceeding critical duration (*Henbane, Wheat, Radish*). A red flash during night **promotes** flowering.
- **Day-Neutral Plants (DNP)**: Flowering is independent of photoperiod (*Tomato, Sunflower, Cucumber, Maize*).

### 9.2 Phytochrome Photoreceptor & Florigen
- **Phytochrome**: Blue-green chromoprotein in leaves. Exists as $\text{P}_r$ (absorbs $660\text{ nm}$, inactive) and $\text{P}_{fr}$ (absorbs $730\text{ nm}$, biologically active).
- **Florigen**: Systemic flowering signal (FT protein) synthesized in leaves under inductive photoperiods and transported via phloem to the shoot apex.

### 9.3 Vernalization (Cold Temperature Induction)
- Requirement for low temperature ($1\text{--}10^\circ\text{C}$) to induce flowering in winter annuals (*Wheat, Barley*) and biennials (*Cabbage, Sugarbeet*).
- **Perception Site**: Actively dividing meristematic cells (shoot apical meristem or embryo).
- **Epigenetic Mechanism**: Cold exposure epigenetically silences the floral repressor gene *FLC* (*Flowering Locus C*).

sections.title: High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Exam Traps
sections.topic: 10 Critical Diagnostic Pitfalls in Plant Development & Phytohormones

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Review these 10 high-yield exam traps to avoid common negative marking pitfalls in NEST and INBO.

sections.content:
### High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Exam Traps

| Misconception / Trap | Biological Reality | Exam Tip / Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *"Short-day plants measure the length of the light period to flower."* | Short-day plants measure the **uninterrupted length of the DARK period (Night length)**. | A brief flash of red light during the night prevents flowering in SDPs. |
| *"Auxin promotes cell elongation by making the cytoplasm acidic."* | Auxins trigger $\text{H}^+$-ATPase pumps to acidify the **CELL WALL space (extracellular matrix)**, activating expansins. | Acid growth hypothesis applies to cell walls, not the cytoplasm. |
| *"Abscisic Acid promotes stomatal opening under intense light."* | ABA triggers **STOMATAL CLOSURE** under water stress by inducing $\text{K}^+$ efflux from guard cells. | ABA is the stress hormone; cytokinins/auxins promote stomatal opening. |
| *"Ethylene is a liquid phytohormone applied as Ethephon."* | Ethylene is a **GASEOUS hormone ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$)**. Ethephon is an aqueous compound that releases ethylene gas inside tissues. | Ethylene is the only gaseous phytohormone. |
| *"Cytokinin and Auxin work synergistically to maintain apical dominance."* | Cytokinin and Auxin act **ANTAGONISTICALLY** in apical dominance: Auxin maintains apical dominance; Cytokinin overcomes it. | Cytokinins stimulate lateral axillary bud growth. |
| *"Vernalization stimulus is perceived by mature photosynthetic leaves."* | Vernalization (cold) is perceived by **actively dividing meristems (SAM or embryo)**. Photoperiodism is perceived by leaves. | Do not confuse photoperiodic leaves with vernalization meristems. |
| *"Arithmetic growth produces a sigmoidal S-shaped growth curve."* | Arithmetic growth produces a **LINEAR curve ($L_t = L_0 + rt$)**. Geometric growth produces a **SIGMOIDAL S-curve ($W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$)**. | $2^n$ geometric growth features lag, log, and stationary phases. |
| *"$\text{P}_{fr}$ is the inactive form of phytochrome that accumulates in the dark."* | **$\text{P}_{fr}$ is the ACTIVE form** generated by red light ($660\text{ nm}$). In the dark, $\text{P}_{fr}$ slowly reverts back to inactive $\text{P}_r$. | $\text{P}_{fr}$ absorbs far-red light ($730\text{ nm}$). |
| *"Dedifferentiation refers to meristematic cells becoming mature functional tissues."* | Mature tissue becoming meristematic is **DEDIFFERENTIATION**. Meristematic cells becoming mature is **DIFFERENTIATION**. | Formation of interfascicular cambium is an example of dedifferentiation. |
| *"Gibberellins induce bolting in woody trees during autumn."* | Gibberellins induce bolting (internodal elongation) in **ROSETTE plants (*Cabbage, Sugarbeet*)** prior to flowering. | $\text{GA}_3$ overcomes dwarfism in rosette plants. |

sections.title: Master Glossary for Plant Development
sections.topic: 35+ Definitive Terms & Concepts for Olympiads & NEST

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Complete glossary covering plant growth, hormonal terms, development kinetics, and photoperiodic definitions.

sections.content:
### Master Glossary for Plant Growth & Development

- **Abscisic Acid (ABA)**: A 15-carbon sesquiterpenoid phytohormone that induces stomatal closure, maintains seed dormancy, and mediates stress responses.
- **Absolute Growth Rate (AGR)**: Total growth or biomass increment per unit time ($\frac{\Delta W}{\Delta t}$).
- **Acid Growth Hypothesis**: Model proposing that auxin activates $\text{H}^+$-ATPase pumps to acidify cell walls, activating expansins to loosen wall matrix bonds.
- **Aleurone Layer**: The protein-rich outer cell layer of cereal endosperm that synthesizes hydrolytic enzymes ($\alpha$-amylase) in response to gibberellins.
- **Apical Dominance**: The phenomenon where high auxin levels produced by the shoot apex inhibit the growth of lateral axillary buds.
- **Arithmetic Growth**: A pattern of growth where one daughter cell remains meristematic while the other differentiates, yielding a linear curve ($L_t = L_0 + rt$).
- **Auxin**: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and related compounds that promote cell elongation, apical dominance, and adventitious rooting.
- **Avena Curvature Test**: A quantitative bioassay for auxins measuring the angle of curvature in decapitated oat coleoptiles.
- **Bakanae Disease**: "Foolish seedling" disease of rice caused by *Gibberella fujikuroi*, which led to the discovery of gibberellins.
- **Bolting**: The dramatic internodal elongation of a stem in rosette plants prior to flowering, induced by gibberellins.
- **Callus**: An undifferentiated mass of proliferating parenchymatous cells formed in tissue culture.
- **Caulogenesis**: The differentiation of shoot buds from cultured callus tissue under a high cytokinin to low auxin ratio.
- **Climacteric Ripening**: A rapid spike in respiration and ethylene evolution accompanying the ripening of certain fruits.
- **Cytokinin**: $N^6$-substituted adenine derivatives (e.g., Zeatin, Kinetin) that promote cell division, shoot initiation, and delay senescence.
- **Dedifferentiation**: The process by which mature, non-dividing differentiated cells regain meristematic division capacity.
- **Development**: The sum of all structural and physiological changes an organism undergoes throughout its life cycle (Growth + Differentiation).
- **Differentiation**: The structural and functional specialization of meristematic cells into mature permanent cells.
- **Epigeal Germination**: Germination where rapid hypocotyl elongation pulls the cotyledons above the soil surface.
- **Ethephon**: An aqueous organosilicon compound (2-chloroethylphosphonic acid) that releases ethylene gas inside plant tissues.
- **Ethylene**: A simple gaseous phytohormone ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$) that promotes fruit ripening, triple response, and abscission.
- **Expansin**: A class of cell-wall-loosening proteins activated by acidic pH that disrupt hydrogen bonds between cellulose microfibrils.
- **Florigen**: The systemic flowering signal (FT protein) synthesized in leaves under inductive photoperiods and transported to the shoot apex.
- **Geometric Growth**: A pattern of growth where all daughter cells retain division capacity, yielding a sigmoidal S-curve ($W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$).
- **Gibberellin**: Diterpenoid phytohormones (e.g., $\text{GA}_3$) that promote internodal elongation, seed germination, and enzyme induction.
- **Heterophylly**: The occurrence of different leaf shapes on the same plant due to developmental phases or environmental conditions (Plasticity).
- **Hypogeal Germination**: Germination where epicotyl elongation leaves cotyledons below the soil surface.
- **Imbibition**: The initial passive absorption of water by dry hydrophilic colloids (e.g., seed coats) causing swelling.
- **Kinetin**: A synthetic cytokinin ($N^6$-furfurylaminopurine) isolated from autoclaved herring sperm DNA.
- **Long-Day Plant (LDP)**: A plant that flowers when light duration exceeds a specific critical threshold.
- **Parthenocarpy**: The development of seedless fruits without prior ovular fertilization.
- **Phytochrome**: A dimeric chromoprotein photoreceptor that exists in interconvertible $\text{P}_r$ ($660\text{ nm}$) and $\text{P}_{fr}$ ($730\text{ nm}$) forms.
- **Plasticity**: The capacity of a plant to alter its development or morphology in response to environmental cues.
- **Polar Auxin Transport (PAT)**: The directional cell-to-cell movement of auxin mediated by polarly localized PIN efflux carriers.
- **Quiescence**: A state of delayed germination imposed purely by unfavorable environmental conditions (lack of water/warmth).
- **Redifferentiation**: The process where dedifferentiated secondary meristematic cells lose division capacity to form mature secondary tissues.
- **Relative Growth Rate (RGR)**: Growth rate per unit time expressed relative to initial measurement/biomass.
- **Rhizogenesis**: The differentiation of adventitious roots from callus tissue under a high auxin to low cytokinin ratio.
- **Richmond-Lang Effect**: The delay of leaf senescence and chlorophyll breakdown induced by cytokinin application.
- **Scarification**: Mechanical or chemical abrasion of impermeable seed coats to break physical dormancy.
- **Short-Day Plant (SDP)**: A plant that flowers when the uninterrupted dark night period exceeds a critical threshold.
- **Stratification**: The cold, moist temperature treatment ($0\text{--}5^\circ\text{C}$) of seeds to break physiological dormancy.
- **Triple Response**: A diagnostic seedling response to ethylene characterized by hypocotyl shortening, radial swelling, and apical hook formation.
- **Vernalization**: The induction of flowering by a prolonged period of low temperature treatment ($1\text{--}10^\circ\text{C}$).
- **Zeatin**: A naturally occurring cytokinin isolated from corn kernels (*Zea mays*) and coconut milk.

chapterCommonMistakes: Short-day plants measure light length (Reality: They measure the uninterrupted length of the DARK period / long night).
Auxin acidifies the cytoplasm (Reality: Acidifies the extracellular cell wall space to activate expansins).
ABA opens stomata in bright light (Reality: ABA triggers stomatal CLOSURE via K⁺/Cl⁻ efflux under water stress).
Ethylene is a liquid hormone (Reality: Gaseous hormone; Ethephon is the aqueous formulation releasing gas).
Cytokinin and Auxin work synergistically in apical dominance (Reality: Antagonistic; Auxin maintains, Cytokinin overcomes).
Vernalization is perceived by leaves (Reality: Perceived by actively dividing meristems / embryos; leaves perceive photoperiod).
Arithmetic growth produces an S-curve (Reality: Linear curve Lt = L0 + rt; geometric produces sigmoidal S-curve).
Pfr is the inactive phytochrome (Reality: Pfr is the active form generated by 660 nm red light).
Dedifferentiation is meristem turning into mature tissue (Reality: Mature tissue regaining meristematic division).
Gibberellins induce bolting in woody trees in autumn (Reality: Induce internodal elongation in rosette plants like cabbage).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A plant physiologist performs a tissue culture experiment using tobacco pith parenchyma. When the culture medium contains an Auxin-to-Cytokinin concentration ratio of 100:1, rapid proliferation of an undifferentiated cell mass occurs. What morphogenic transition will be observed if the researcher adjusts the hormone concentrations to an Auxin-to-Cytokinin ratio of 1:100?

options.text: Induction of intense root differentiation (Rhizogenesis)
Induction of adventitious shoot bud differentiation (Caulogenesis)
Complete suppression of all cell division and entry into G0 phase
Immediate synthesis of α-amylase and seed coat scarification

questions.solutionExplanation: According to the Skoog and Miller organogenesis model, a High Auxin : Low Cytokinin ratio promotes rooting (Rhizogenesis), whereas a Low Auxin : High Cytokinin ratio (1:100) shifts morphogenic fate to promote shoot bud differentiation (Caulogenesis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In a photoperiodism experiment, a Short-Day Plant (SDP) with a critical night length of 10 hours is exposed to a 12-hour light period followed by a 12-hour dark period. However, during the 6th hour of darkness, the plant is exposed to a 5-second flash of red light (660 nm). What will be the floral response of this plant?

options.text: It will flower normally because total darkness exceeded 10 hours.
It will fail to flower because the critical long night was interrupted by red light, converting inactive Pr to active Pfr.
It will flower precociously due to rapid florigen accumulation.
It will undergo immediate vernalization and produce male flowers only.

questions.solutionExplanation: Short-Day Plants are strictly Long-Night Plants; they require an uninterrupted dark period exceeding their critical night length. A flash of red light (660 nm) during the dark period converts inactive Pr into active Pfr, which resets the biological clock and inhibits flowering in SDPs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: During cereal seed germination, which specific tissue layer secretes α-amylase in response to Embryo-derived Gibberellins (GA3), and what transcription factor is de-repressed to activate α-amylase gene expression?

options.text: Scutellum; p53
Aleurone Layer; GAMYB
Pericarp; E2F
Coleoptile; PIN1

questions.solutionExplanation: Gibberellins (GA3) synthesized by the germinating embryo diffuse into the Aleurone Layer of the endosperm, where they bind receptors that de-repress the GAMYB transcription factor, activating transcription and secretion of α-Amylase to hydrolyze endosperm starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic: Submerged Rice Stem Elongation by Ethylene
questions.questionText: A batch of deep-water rice plants experiencing seasonal flood submergence undergoes a sudden 5-fold acceleration in petiole and internodal stem elongation, allowing their upper leaves to remain above the rising water surface. Which phytohormone mediates this rapid submerged stem elongation response?

options.text: Abscisic Acid (ABA)
Ethylene
Cytokinin
Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA)

questions.solutionExplanation: Submergence traps the gaseous hormone Ethylene inside deep-water rice tissues. Accumulated ethylene triggers rapid petiole and internodal stem elongation, keeping the photosynthetic leaf canopy above water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A cell population undergoing geometric growth expands according to the equation W1 = W0 e^(rt). If an initial plant tissue mass of 10 grams expands to 80 grams over a period of 6 days of exponential growth, what is the relative growth rate (r) of the tissue in days⁻¹? (Take ln 2 ≈ 0.693)

options.text: 0.115 day⁻¹
0.693 day⁻¹
2.079 day⁻¹

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What is the biochemical precursor and essential trace metal ion required for the endogenous biosynthesis of Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA / Auxin) in plants?

options.text: L-Methionine; Iron (Fe²⁺)
L-Tryptophan; Zinc (Zn²⁺)
Mevalonic Acid; Magnesium (Mg²⁺)
Adenine; Copper (Cu²⁺)

questions.solutionExplanation: Auxin (IAA) is biosynthesized from the amino acid L-Tryptophan via indole-3-pyruvic acid in a pathway requiring Zinc (Zn²⁺) as an essential enzyme co-factor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which plant growth regulator is commonly sprayed on commercial sugarcane crops to increase stem length and boost sugar yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre?

options.text: Abscisic Acid (ABA)
Gibberellin (GA3)
Zeatin
2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D)

questions.solutionExplanation: Spraying sugarcane fields with Gibberellins (GA3) stimulates dramatic internodal stem elongation, increasing total stem biomass and raising sugar yields significantly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: When a plant experiences severe soil drought, roots synthesize Abscisic Acid (ABA) which translocates to leaves. How does ABA trigger rapid stomatal closure in guard cells?

options.text: By activating H⁺-ATPase pumps to acidify guard cell cytoplasm
By stimulating Ca²⁺ influx into cytosol, triggering massive efflux of K⁺ and Cl⁻ ions and loss of turgor
By promoting Malate synthesis inside guard cell vacuoles
By inducing rapid cell division in subsidiary cells

questions.solutionExplanation: ABA binds guard cell membrane receptors, opening hyperpolarization-activated Ca²⁺ channels. Elevated cytosolic Ca²⁺ depolarizes the membrane and activates anion/cation channels, driving a massive efflux of K⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Water leaves guard cells osmotically, leading to loss of turgor and stomatal closure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The phenomenon where mature, non-dividing cortical parenchyma cells regain mitotic division capacity to form the cork cambium (phellogen) during secondary growth is an example of:

options.text: Primary Differentiation
Dedifferentiation
Redifferentiation
Developmental Plasticity

questions.solutionExplanation: Mature, differentiated permanent cells (cortex parenchyma) regaining mitotic division potential to form secondary meristems (cork cambium) is Dedifferentiation. (When phellogen produces cork cells that lose division capacity, that is Redifferentiation).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which commercial synthetic phytohormone formulation is widely applied to agricultural crops as a selective herbicide to eliminate broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds from monocotyledonous cereal fields?

options.text: α-Naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA)
2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D)
Ethephon
Kinetin

questions.solutionExplanation: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used extensively as a selective herbicide. Dicotyledonous weeds absorb 2,4-D rapidly and undergo lethal uncontrolled growth, whereas monocotyledonous cereal crops metabolize or exclude 2,4-D and remain unharmed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following physiological responses are driven by Auxins? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Induction of apical dominance by suppressing axillary bud outgrowth
Cell elongation via activation of plasma membrane H⁺-ATPase proton pumps (Acid Growth Hypothesis)
Delay of leaf senescence via the Richmond-Lang effect
Promotion of adventitious root initiation in stem cuttings

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, D are correct: Auxins mediate apical dominance, cell elongation via acid growth wall loosening, and root initiation in cuttings. C is incorrect: Delay of leaf senescence via nutrient mobilization (Richmond-Lang Effect) is a diagnostic role of Cytokinins, NOT auxins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following developmental events are regulated by Gibberellins (GA)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Induction of bolting (internodal elongation) in rosette plants like cabbage
De-repression of GAMYB to induce α-Amylase synthesis in cereal aleurone layers
Maintenance of seed dormancy during freezing winter conditions
Elongation of grape stalks and improvement of apple fruit shape

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, D are correct: Gibberellins promote bolting, induce aleurone α-amylase, and elongate grape stalks/fruit shapes. C is incorrect: Seed dormancy is maintained by Abscisic Acid (ABA), which is an antagonist to gibberellins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the valid statements regarding the gaseous phytohormone Ethylene: (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is biosynthesized from L-Methionine via the intermediate 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC).
It induces the "Triple Response" in etiolated seedlings (hypocotyl shortening, radial swelling, apical hook formation).
Ethephon is an aqueous formulation that releases ethylene gas inside plant tissues.
It suppresses female flower determination (pistillate) in monoecious cucumbers.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: Ethylene is derived from Methionine via ACC, causes the triple response, and is commercially supplied as Ethephon. D is incorrect: Ethylene PROMOTES (increases) female flower determination in monoecious cucumbers, enhancing fruit yield.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions describe the Stress Hormone Abscisic Acid (ABA)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is biosynthesized via oxidative cleavage of carotenoid xanthophylls (violaxanthin).
It acts as a direct biochemical antagonist to Gibberellins (GA) in seed dormancy and amylase expression.
It induces rapid stomatal closure by triggering K⁺ and Cl⁻ ion efflux from guard cells.
It accelerates the malting process in barley brewing industries.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: ABA is derived from xanthophylls, antagonizes GA to maintain dormancy, and closes stomata. D is incorrect: Accelerating malting in barley is performed by Gibberellins (GA3), which induce amylase; ABA inhibits this process.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct statements regarding Photoperiodism and Phytochrome Action: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Short-Day Plants (SDP) require an uninterrupted dark night period exceeding a critical threshold to flower.
The photoperiodic stimulus is perceived exclusively by mature photosynthetic leaves.
Red light (660 nm) converts inactive Pr into biologically active Pfr.
Florigen is a lipid-soluble steroid hormone synthesized in the shoot apical meristem.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: SDPs measure uninterrupted night length, leaves perceive photoperiod, and red light converts Pr -> Pfr. D is incorrect: Florigen is a protein (FT protein / Flowering Locus T) synthesized in leaves (NOT meristems) that translocates via phloem to the apex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following represent valid examples of Plant Plasticity and Heterophylly? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Developmental heterophylly in Cotton, Coriander, and Larkspur where juvenile and adult leaves differ in shape.
Environmental heterophylly in Buttercup (Ranunculus flabellaris) where aquatic submerged leaves are dissected while aerial leaves are broad.
Formation of a cell plate during cytokinesis in plant cells.
Transition of shoot apical meristem into a floral meristem upon vernalization.

questions.solutionExplanation: A and B are correct: Heterophylly in Cotton/Coriander (developmental) and Buttercup (environmental) are classic examples of Plasticity. C and D are incorrect: Cytokinesis and vernalization are general developmental processes, not examples of leaf plasticity/heterophylly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which phytohormones act as primary inhibitors of leaf senescence and defoliation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Cytokinin (delays senescence via Richmond-Lang effect)
Ethylene
Auxin (prevents premature leaf drop at early stages)
Abscisic Acid

questions.solutionExplanation: A and C are correct: Cytokinins (Richmond-Lang effect) and Auxins (at early stages) prevent premature leaf senescence and abscission. B and D are incorrect: Ethylene and Abscisic Acid are primary promoters of senescence, defoliation, and abscission.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding Vernalization are TRUE? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Vernalization is the induction of flowering by a period of low temperature treatment (1–10°C).
The cold stimulus is perceived strictly by actively dividing meristematic cells in the shoot apex or embryo.
Vernalization prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season.
Vernalization occurs exclusively in desert CAM plants.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, C are correct: Vernalization is cold induction (1–10°C), perceived by meristems/embryos, preventing premature winter flowering in winter annuals and biennials. D is incorrect: Vernalization is characteristic of winter annuals (wheat, barley) and biennials (cabbage, carrot), NOT desert CAM succulents.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following growth measurements are characteristic of Geometric Growth? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Equal cell division capacity retained by both daughter cells (2ⁿ progression).
Growth curve displays Lag, Log/Exponential, and Stationary phases.
Represented mathematically by Lt = L0 + rt.
Displayed by embryonic cells during early cleavage and unicellular populations in unlimited media.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, D are correct: Geometric growth exhibits 2ⁿ proliferation, a sigmoidal S-curve (lag, log, stationary phases), and occurs in early embryos/microbes. C is incorrect: Lt = L0 + rt represents Arithmetic Growth (linear). Geometric growth is W1 = W0 e^(rt).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct options regarding seed germination and dormancy breakage: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Scarification breaks physical seed dormancy by chipping impermeable seed coats.
Stratification involves moist cold temperature treatment (0–5°C) to lower ABA and elevate GA levels.
Imbibition is an active ATP-dependent process requiring high metabolic respiration.
Red light (660 nm) promotes germination in photoblastic lettuce seeds by converting Pr to Pfr.

questions.solutionExplanation: A, B, D are correct: Scarification breaks seed coat dormancy, stratification uses cold moist treatment to shift ABA/GA balance, and red light activates photoblastic germination via Pfr. C is incorrect: Imbibition is a PASSIVE physical process (adsorption of water by dry hydrophilic seed colloids) that occurs independently of cellular respiration or ATP.
